articles.title: Android app developers will soon have to share their address publicly
articles.short_snippet: Independent Android app developers are worried about their privacy after Google announced that from next year many of them will be required to share a phone number and address publicly. The policy change is intended to meet European Union regulations under the Digital Services Act, but Google says contact details will be made public worldwide. […]

articles.short_snippet: US District Judge Loren AliKhan has blocked the Federal Communications Commission from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses in a preliminary injunction, and rejected its efforts to dismiss ABC's First Amendment lawsuit. ABC has accused the FCC of violating its free speech rights and claims the agency "waged a retaliatory campaign" against the […]

articles.short_snippet: Black Friday isn’t just a good time to save on a new TV but also a chance to spend less on what you watch on it. articles.title: DRAM contract prices stay high as supply-demand squeeze persists
articles.short_snippet: The Taiwan Institute of Economic Research (TIER) said on October 25 that strong AI chip demand is keeping advanced process capacity fully utilized, while tight global DRAM supply and demand are supporting high contract prices and lifting manufacturers' revenue through rising shipments of customized products. articles.title: Samsung Display may remain sole iPhone Duo panel supplier for five years
articles.short_snippet: Samsung Display (SDC) could remain Apple's sole supplier of foldable OLED panels for at least five years, beyond the term of a reported three-year exclusive supply agreement, as rival manufacturers struggle to match its technology and production capabilities.

articles.title: SK Hynix seeks TSMC 3nm expertise as Micron steps up hiring
articles.short_snippet: SK Hynix is seeking engineers with experience in TSMC's 3nm process to develop customized high-bandwidth memory (HBM), while US rival Micron Technology is stepping up recruitment in South Korea to support its Asian expansion.

articles.title: Samsung, DB HiTek eye 8-inch foundry price hikes as AI demand surges
articles.short_snippet: Major semiconductor foundries using 8-inch (200mm) wafers are operating at or near full capacity and seeking further price increases as demand for power chips used in AI data centers grows and major chipmakers scale back older production lines.

articles.title: Xpeng targets 2026 year-end mass production for Iron humanoid robot
articles.short_snippet: Chinese electric vehicle (EV) maker Xpeng held its AI Day 2026 in Guangzhou, China, on November 25, sharing its latest developments in physical artificial intelligence (AI), with its Iron humanoid robot. The company plans to begin mass production by the end of 2026.

articles.title: Chip substrate makers face 30-month waits for key equipment
articles.short_snippet: Delivery times for some equipment used to manufacture advanced chip substrates have stretched from six months to 30 months as manufacturers race to expand production to meet surging demand for artificial intelligence (AI) chips.

articles.title: Micron, Samsung, SK Hynix strike multiyear memory deals
articles.short_snippet: The world's three largest memory chipmakers are securing multiyear supply agreements as shortages driven by AI demand push customers to commit cash years before chips are delivered.

articles.title: Nvidia reportedly halts server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries as new US chip rule bites
articles.short_snippet: Nvidia has told its manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia, the Financial Times ( FT ) reported on November 26, as a new US rule against Chinese companies' rented access to AI computing hits the region's data center boom and governments there race to show Washington they will comply.

articles.title: CBTech launches TGV foundry production line, secures sample orders from 5 major customers
articles.short_snippet: Precision exposure equipment maker Chime Ball Technology (CBTech) announced on November 25 that Taiwan's first full-process foundry production line for through glass via (TGV) and glass core substrates (GCS) has been completed and has begun operations at its headquarters in Luzhu, Taoyuan.

articles.title: Intel lawsuit details Trump's push for US$8.9 billion stake
articles.short_snippet: A US Commerce Department lawyer warned Intel's management in August 2025 against treating a proposed government equity stake as a negotiation, according to internal company records cited in a shareholder lawsuit and reported by Wired .

articles.title: Commentary: Taiwan supply chains monitor Trump's potential interference with Nvidia
articles.short_snippet: Nvidia's board agreed to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang, prompting stock markets in the US, Japan, South Korea and Taiwan to rally. After the one-day surge, US President Donald Trump claimed credit for the board's decision, raising concerns that his governing style could lead him to seek something in return from Nvidia or Huang.

articles.title: Exclusive: AI supply chain faces shipment delays as KYC expands
articles.short_snippet: The US Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) export control rules, effective November 19, 2026, expand customer reviews and shipment restrictions across the AI server supply chain. articles.title: China scales, Japan supplies, Korea builds — three AI playbooks behind a 60%-plus grip on the global PCB market
articles.short_snippet: Growing global investment in AI infrastructure is lifting demand for high-end printed circuit boards (PCBs), IC substrates and high-speed interconnects, and Asia's leading PCB makers are speeding up changes to their product lines and capacity. The Taiwan Printed Circuit Association (TPCA) says China, Japan and South Korea are each using their own industrial strengths to build up supply chains for

articles.title: Huang is back in Nvidia, but Washington's chip squeeze on China is only tightening
articles.short_snippet: After just 11 days away from the job, Jensen Huang is back at the helm of Nvidia, the maker of the world's most advanced AI chips. However, his return has so far not changed the momentum of an unfolding US political crackdown on Chinese access to advanced chips. Instead, China's access to advanced AI compute is narrowing on several fronts at once as the market reacts to new American rules.

articles.short_snippet: Shanghai Party Secretary Chen Jining is reportedly under investigation. The news has sent a shock through one of China's key technology hubs and its political and business circles. articles.title: Amazon Leo launches 36 satellites but struggles to close gap with Starlink
articles.short_snippet: Amazon's satellite internet initiative, Amazon Leo, has successfully launched another 36 low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites aboard Europe's Ariane 6 rocket, advancing its long-delayed commercial service rollout.

articles.title: Tata Electronics reportedly opens talks with contractors for phase 2 of Assam chip packaging plant
articles.short_snippet: Tata Electronics is lining up the second phase of its semiconductor assembly and test plant in Assam before the facility has been formally inaugurated, extending a project described as India's first indigenous semiconductor assembly and test facility.

articles.title: Huawei offers free chip patent licenses to take on Nvidia
articles.short_snippet: Huawei Technologies is offering free patent licenses for its UnifiedBus chip interconnect technology and has set up dedicated semiconductor and artificial intelligence (AI) patent teams as it seeks to attract overseas hardware suppliers and build a computing ecosystem to rival Nvidia's.

articles.title: US warns of memory glut as Samsung, SK Hynix expand
articles.short_snippet: The US has warned that South Korea's government-backed memory chip expansion could lead to a glut even as AI demand strains global supplies. The findings name Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, although memory chips are excluded from the proposed tariffs.

articles.title: SpaceX's million-satellite approval pushes AI infrastructure into a new supply-chain frontier
articles.short_snippet: As aggressive AI infrastructure buildouts continue to stretch the limits of power availability, land, and thermal management, SpaceX's longstanding ambition to extend the competitive boundaries of AI computing beyond Earth is moving closer to realization.

articles.title: SK Hynix eyes 100-layer 3D DRAM production by 2031
articles.short_snippet: SK Hynix aims to mass-produce 100-layer 3D DRAM within four to five years as the South Korean chipmaker looks to overcome the limits of conventional memory scaling.

articles.title: Trump's overcapacity tariffs target chips, EVs, solar in 14 economies; China calls it 'false proposition'
articles.short_snippet: The Trump administration plans to impose new tariffs on 14 major trading partners over alleged "excess capacity," with China among the main targets.

articles.title: BOE eyes Visionox takeover as CNY4.6 billion funding crunch looms
articles.short_snippet: China's display giant BOE Technology is considering acquiring fellow panel maker Visionox, expanding the target from a single OLED production line to the entire company. Reports from The Elec and DealSite said BOE executives and senior officials from the Hefei municipal government have met to discuss the deal, with the scope of the acquisition expected to be finalized in December 2026.

articles.title: Topco Technologies targets double-digit AI materials revenue share
articles.short_snippet: Topco Technologies aims to raise AI materials to a double-digit share of revenue from current levels of 9% to 10%, while expanding into materials for humanoid robots, advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), energy storage, and cosmetics, chairman Chen-cheng Pan said. The company expects its optical communications materials business to become clearer in the second half of 2027.

articles.title: How new US export controls and fragile trade truces triggered sell-off in China's domestic GPU sector
articles.short_snippet: On November 25, 2026, China's leading domestic GPU developers, including MetaX, Moore Threads, Biren Technology, and Iluvatar CoreX, suffered a sharp, synchronized sell-off. By market close, three of the four stocks hit all-time lows.

articles.title: Japan reportedly weighs supply chain diversification requirements for critical goods
articles.short_snippet: Japan is considering requiring companies that depend on semiconductors and other strategically important products to diversify their supply chains, as the government seeks to strengthen economic security and reduce reliance on individual countries and suppliers.

articles.title: Nvidia leadership turmoil puts customer due diligence in spotlight across AI supply chain
articles.short_snippet: Know your customer (KYC) has become a buzzword across the AI supply chain following the recent controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Suppliers are increasingly cautious about crossing geopolitical red lines while seeking to avoid financial risks arising from hastily accepted orders.

articles.title: YMTC now licenses NAND tech to Samsung, SK Hynix: Inside the Xtacking patent wall reshaping 400-layer memory
articles.short_snippet: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are adopting parts of Xtacking, the 3D NAND stacking technology first developed by China's Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. (YMTC), through cross-licensing deals. Nikkei Asia reported the arrangement, citing three people briefed on the matter. A Chinese company founded only a decade ago is now licensing technology to the world's two largest memory makers.

articles.title: HP and Dell see weak PC market as memory prices rise in 2027
articles.short_snippet: HP and Dell, two leading US PC brands, expect memory prices to continue rising in 2027, though at a slower pace, while warning that the PC market will remain weak. HP said the corporate PC replacement cycle has largely ended, with the downturn that began in the second half of 2026 extending into 2027.

articles.title: Resonac targets 2027 production of photosensitive film for panel packaging
articles.short_snippet: Resonac has developed a photosensitive insulating film for panel-level semiconductor packaging, targeting mass production in 2027 as chipmakers look to larger package formats for high-performance devices.
